title: Outlook: reply with a template in inbox rules
summary: Hold: the licensing paragraph omits Microsoft's exception for secondary accounts and incorrectly says its source does not address Outlook on the web. The page also overstates the mailbox policy as the only existing control, despite documented automation for disabling individual inbox rules.

claims.where: title; summary; What's changing; Scope
claims.claim: The new capability lets users of new Outlook for Windows and Outlook on the web create inbox rules that reply using a saved template.
claims.quote: Users of new Outlook for Windows and Outlook on the web will be able to create inbox rules that automatically reply to incoming messages using a saved template.

claims.where: What's changing; Why it matters; Risk assessment: Data exposure
claims.claim: Users choose the conditions for incoming messages.
claims.quote: Set the conditions you care about and pick the template, and Outlook handles the response for you.

claims.where: What's changing; Why it matters; Risk assessment: Data exposure
claims.claim: Users select the saved template that supplies the automatic response.
claims.quote: Users can select a saved template as the automatic reply.

claims.where: What's changing; Why it matters; Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions
claims.claim: When an incoming message meets the rule conditions, Outlook automatically sends the template without approval of each reply.
claims.quote: When an incoming message meets the rule conditions, Outlook automatically sends the configured template response.

claims.where: What's changing
claims.claim: Microsoft Learn has no page describing this new Outlook and web template-reply rule feature at the time of writing.
claims.quote: Searched: new Outlook Outlook on the web reply with a template inbox rules action admin disable policy RulesEnabled; new Outlook reply with template inbox rule sender identity external automatic repeat replies limits. Opened policy-management and emulate-out-of-office-assistant; the latter is Rules Wizard.

claims.where: front matter: defaultState; Why it matters; rationale: risk and impact
claims.claim: The capability is user-opt-in: sending these replies depends on a user creating the rule, rather than automatic creation of a reply rule at rollout.
claims.quote: Users can create an inbox rule with conditions for incoming messages. Users can select a saved template as the automatic reply. When an incoming message meets the rule conditions, Outlook automatically sends the configured template response.

claims.where: Why it matters
claims.claim: Outlook sends the automatic response in the user's name.
claims.quote: Searched: new Outlook reply with template inbox rule sender identity external automatic repeat replies limits. Read MC1505607, the roadmap, policy-management and emulate-out-of-office-assistant; none identifies the sending identity for this new feature.
claims.fix: Remove 'in the user's name' from the sentence; neither the roadmap nor MC1505607 states the sending identity.

claims.where: controls[0].ui; Governance controls table
claims.claim: The Inbox Rules control is reached in the Exchange admin center through Roles > Outlook web app policies > policy > Features > Manage features > Information management > Inbox Rules.
claims.quote: In the EAC, go to Roles > Outlook web app policies. Features: Select Manage features. Information management. Cited create-policy page: Inbox Rules: If set to Enabled, a user can create and edit custom rules in Outlook on the web and the new Outlook for Windows.

claims.where: controls[0].api; Governance controls table
claims.claim: Exchange PowerShell supports Set-OwaMailboxPolicy -Identity <policy name> -RulesEnabled $false to disable users' rule management.
claims.quote: The Identity parameter specifies the Outlook on the web mailbox policy that you want to modify. $false: Users can't view, create, or modify server-side rules in Outlook on the web.

claims.where: controls[0].governs; Why it matters; Risk assessment; Governance guidance; rationale: risk
claims.claim: The Inbox Rules mailbox-policy setting governs creation and editing of custom rules in Outlook on the web and new Outlook for Windows, not just the new action.
claims.quote: Inbox Rules: If set to Enabled, a user can create and edit custom rules in Outlook on the web and the new Outlook for Windows.

claims.where: controls[0].note; Scope: Mailbox policy default; Governance controls
claims.claim: RulesEnabled defaults to $true.
claims.quote: $true: Users can view, create, or modify server-side rules in Outlook on the web. This value is the default.

claims.where: controls[0].note; Governance controls
claims.claim: The RulesEnabled reference describes management of server-side rules in Outlook on the web.
claims.quote: The RulesEnabled parameter specifies whether a user can view, create, or modify server-side rules in Outlook on the web.

claims.where: Governance guidance: At rollout; Governance controls
claims.claim: Outlook on the web mailbox-policy changes may take up to 60 minutes to take effect.
claims.quote: Changes to Outlook on the web mailbox policies might take up to 60 minutes to take effect.

claims.where: Governance controls
claims.claim: The RulesEnabled reference does not say what happens to the execution of existing rules when rule management is disabled.
claims.quote: Searched: RulesEnabled and reply/template in the fetched Set-OwaMailboxPolicy reference; read the RulesEnabled description and both Boolean values. It describes viewing, creating and modifying server-side rules, not execution of existing rules.

claims.where: controls[1]; Why it matters; Governance controls; front matter: changes
claims.claim: Microsoft Learn documents no separate UI or automation switch for availability of the reply-with-template action alone.
claims.quote: Searched: new Outlook Outlook on the web reply with a template inbox rules action admin disable policy RulesEnabled; Exchange Online PowerShell Set-OwaMailboxPolicy reply with template action disable inbox rule new Outlook Graph messageRule reply template. Read policy-management and Set-OwaMailboxPolicy.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.model
claims.claim: The licensing model is included in the entitlement Outlook already requires, with no published feature-specific entitlement.
claims.quote: For example, a Business Standard or Business Premium plan provides access to a Microsoft 365 email address and the desktop versions of Outlook and other Microsoft 365 apps.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing: Licence
claims.claim: Using Outlook for Windows with a Microsoft 365 organisational email address requires a plan including desktop Microsoft 365 apps, without stating the secondary-account exception.
claims.quote: Once you add an account with a qualifying license to Outlook, you can add secondary accounts with licenses for products that don't include the desktop apps such as Business Basic or E1.
claims.fix: Add this qualification to the licensing notes and Licence paragraph: 'Once an account with a qualifying desktop-app licence is added, secondary accounts can use licences without desktop apps, such as Business Basic or E1.' Keep the licensing model included and cite https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-365-apps/outlook/get-started/licensing-options.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; rationale: cost
claims.claim: A licence or entitlement specific to this new template-reply action is not yet published.
claims.quote: Searched: Outlook reply with a template inbox rules licensing pricing meter; new Outlook reply with template rule licence entitlement pricing Microsoft 365 Outlook Windows. Opened licensing-options; results describe product licensing or classic Rules Wizard, not an entitlement for this new action.

claims.where: Cost and licensing: Licence
claims.claim: Neither the roadmap nor MC1505607 names another licence for this feature.
claims.quote: Who is affected: Users of new Outlook for Windows and Outlook on the web who use inbox rules and want to automatically reply to incoming messages using saved templates.

claims.where: Cost and licensing: Licence
claims.claim: The new Outlook licensing page does not address Outlook on the web.
claims.quote: The Business Basic plan provides access to productivity tools through the web and mobile versions of Outlook and Microsoft 365.
claims.fix: Replace 'That page covers the new Outlook for Windows app; it does not address Outlook on the web.' with 'The page also states that Business Basic provides access to the web and mobile versions of Outlook and Microsoft 365.'

claims.where: Cost and licensing: Meter; rationale: cost
claims.claim: The roadmap and notice name no feature-specific meter, credit or charge.
claims.quote: You can now create a rule that automatically replies to incoming messages with a template you've set up. Set the conditions you care about and pick the template, and Outlook handles the response for you.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing: Meter
claims.claim: Microsoft has not published a price or meter specific to this new rule action.
claims.quote: Searched: Outlook reply with a template inbox rules licensing pricing meter; new Outlook reply with template rule licence entitlement pricing Microsoft 365 Outlook Windows. Read licensing-options, roadmap and MC1505607; none names an action-specific price or meter.

claims.where: Open questions
claims.claim: The cited remote-domains page names out-of-office messages, administrator-configured automatic replies and inbox-rule forwards, but does not specifically mention inbox-rule template replies.
claims.quote: Searched: template and Inbox rules in the fetched remote-domains page. Read its reply-types table: out-of-office messages, automatic replies set by admins using Set-MailboxAutoReplyConfiguration, and Inbox rules to forward messages; no template-reply rule is named.

claims.where: Why it matters; front matter: changes
claims.claim: The Inbox Rules mailbox-policy setting is the one existing lever and the only documented control.
claims.quote: Use the Disable-InboxRule cmdlet to disable existing Inbox rules in mailboxes.
claims.fix: Change 'The one existing lever is the Inbox Rules setting' to 'An existing lever is the Inbox Rules setting' in Why it matters. In the change note, replace 'as the only documented control' with 'as a documented control'. Retain the narrower statement that no separate switch for availability of this action alone is documented.
